name: ALLOWED
description: Requests allowed by Next-Gen WAF.

name: ABNORMALPATH
description: Abnormal Path indicates that the original path differs from the normalized path.

name: BHH
description: Bad Hop Headers indicate an HTTP smuggling attempt through either a malformed Transfer-Encoding (TE) and/or Content-Length (CL) header, or a well-formed TE and CL header.

name: SQLI
description: SQL Injection is the attempt to gain access to an application or obtain privileged information by executing arbitrary SQL database queries.

name: XSS
description: Cross-Site Scripting is the attempt to hijack a user's account or web-browsing session through malicious JavaScript code.

name: CMDEXE
description: Command Execution is the attempt to gain control or damage a target system through arbitrary system commands by means of user input.

name: LOG4J-JNDI
description: Apache Log4j JNDI remote code execution

name: CODEINJECTION
description: Code Injection is the attempt to gain control or damage a target system through arbitrary application code commands by means of user input. Note, this signal is currently in an experimental phase. Please contact support@signalsciences.com if you ecounter any issues with this signal.

name: IMPOSTOR
description: Search bot impostor is someone pretending to be a Google or Bing search bot, but who is not legitimate. Note, Doesn't depend on a response per se, but needs to be resolved in the cloud first, so shouldn't be used in a pre rule.

name: NOUA
description: Many automated and malicious requests use fake or missing User-Agents to make it difficult to identify the type of device making the requests.

name: FORCEFULBROWSING
description: Forceful Browsing is the failed attempt to access admin pages.

name: DOUBLEENCODING
description: Double Encoding checks for the evasion technique of double encoding html characters.

name: SCANNER
description: Identifies popular scanning services and tools.

name: TRAVERSAL
description: Directory Traversal is the attempt to navigate privileged folders throughout a system in hopes of obtaining sensitive information.

name: BACKDOOR
description: A backdoor signal is a request which attempts to determine if a common backdoor file is present on the system.

name: RESPONSESPLIT
description: Identifies when CRLF characters are submitted as input to the application in order to inject headers into the HTTP response.

name: TORNODE
description: Tor is software that conceals a user's identity. A spike in Tor traffic can indicate an attacker trying to mask their location.

name: SANS
description: When a host becomes compromised, it is commonly used to attack multiple targets, which can trigger it to be recorded as a known malicious IP.

name: SIGSCI-IP
description: An IP that Next-Gen WAF has identified as malicious.

name: DATACENTER
description: Datacenter Traffic is non-organic traffic originating from identified hosting providers. This type of traffic is not commonly associated with a real end user.

name: HTTP4XX
description: 4xx Status Codes commonly refer to client request errors.

name: HTTP403
description: Forbidden. This is commonly seen when the request for a url has been protected by the server's configuration.

name: HTTP404
description: Not Found. This is commonly seen when the request for a page or asset does not exist or cannot be found by the server.

name: HTTP429
description: Too Many Requests. This is commonly seen when rate-limiting is used to slow down the number of active connections to a server.

name: HTTP500
description: Internal Server Error. This is commonly seen when a request generates an unhandled application error.

name: HTTP503
description: Service Unavailable. This is commonly seen when a web service is overloaded or sometimes taken down for maintenance.

name: HTTP5XX
description: 5xx Status Codes commonly refer to server related issues.

name: USERAGENT
description: Attack Tooling is the use of automated software to identify security vulnerabilities or to attempt to exploit a discovered vulnerability.

name: NULLBYTE
description: Null bytes do not normally appear in a request and indicate the request is malformed and potentially malicious.

name: NOTUTF8
description: Invalid Encoding can cause the server to translate malicious characters from a request into a response, causing either a denial of service or XSS.

name: PRIVATEFILE
description: Private files are usually confidential in nature, such as an Apache .htaccess file, or a configuration file which could leak sensitive information.

name: WEAKTLS
description: Weak TLS. A web server's configuration allows SSL/TLS connections to be established with an obsolete cipher suite or protocol version. This signal is based on inspecting a small percent of requests. Also, some architectures and Next-Gen WAF language SDK modules do not support this signal.

name: BLOCKED
description: Requests blocked by Next-Gen WAF.

name: NO-CONTENT-TYPE
description: A POST, PUT or PATCH request that does not have a "Content-Type" request header.  By default application servers should assume "Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii" in this case.  Many automated and malicious requests may be missing "Content Type".

name: MALFORMED-DATA
long_name: Malformed Data in the request body
description: A POST, PUT or PATCH request body that is malformed according to the "Content-Type" request header.  For example, if a "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" request header is specified and contains a POST body that is json.  This is often a programming error, automated or malicious request.  Requires agent 3.2 or higher.

name: COMPRESSED
description: The POST request body is compressed and cannot be inspected.  For example, if a "Content-Encoding: gzip" request header is specified and the POST body is verified to not be plain text. Requires agent 4.30 or higher.

name: UNKNOWN-CONTENT
description: The POST request did not contain a recognized content type, and the inspection engine was unable to guess the type. This may represent a malicious client attempting to implement WAF evasion techniques. Requires agent 4.31 or higher.

name: BODY-PARSER-EVASION
description: A request was made that may not have had its body parsed correctly by the inspection engine. This may represent a malicious client attempting to implement WAF evasion techniques.

name: OOB-DOMAIN
description: Out-of-Band domains are generally used during pentesting to identify vulnerabilities in which network access is allowed.

name: INSECURE-AUTH
description: Insecure Authentication/Authorization, such as using JSON Web Tokens with the None Algorithm.
